import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Determinantal conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinantal_conjecture)
-/

/- Formalisation note: Here, we represent the two normal matrices as $U_1 D_1 U_1^*$ and
$U_2 D_2 U_2^*$ respectively, where $U_1, U_2$ are unitary and $D_1, D_2$
are diagonal. This is an universal form of a normal matrix,
allowing to retrieve $\lambda (A)_i$ as ${D_1}_{i,i}$, whereas the current mathlib
doesn't support obtaining the vector of eigenvalues from a general normal
non-Hermitian matrix. -/

namespace DeterminantalConjecture

/--
Does the determinant of the sum $A + B$ of two $n \times n$ normal
complex matrices $A$ and $B$ always lie in the convex hull
of the $n!$ points $\prod\_i (\lambda(A)\_i + \lambda(B)\_{\sigma(i)})$?
Here the numbers $\lambda(A)\_i$ and $\lambda(B)\_i$ are
the eigenvalues of $A$ and $B$, and $\sigma$ is an element of the symmetric
group $S\_n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 15]
theorem determinantal_conjecture
    (n : Type) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (d1 d2 : n → ℂ) (U1 U2 : unitary (Matrix n n ℂ)) :
    (U1 * Matrix.diagonal d1 * star U1 + U2 * Matrix.diagonal d2 * star U2).det
      ∈ convexHull ℝ { ∏ i, (d1 i + d2 (σ i)) | σ : Equiv.Perm n } := by
  sorry

end DeterminantalConjecture

reformulations.difference: Instead of quantifying over normal matrices A and B and referring to their eigenvalues, Lean quantifies over arbitrary complex diagonal vectors d1, d2 and independent unitary matrices U1, U2, representing the summands as U1·diag(d1)·U1* and U2·diag(d2)·U2*.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The complex spectral theorem says that every normal matrix has such a unitary diagonalization, and conversely every matrix of this form is normal. Unitary similarity preserves the characteristic polynomial, so the diagonal vectors list exactly the eigenvalues, with algebraic multiplicity. Reordering either eigenvalue list leaves the permutation-product set unchanged: after reordering d1 by τ and d2 by ρ, reindex the product and replace σ by ρ∘σ∘τ⁻¹. Thus the parameterization neither restricts nor strengthens the conjecture. Normality, the characteristic-polynomial identity, and invariance of the vertex set under reordering were checked in Lean; the full equivalence using the converse spectral theorem was not formalized in the scratch files.

review.notes: Checked the sole declaration against the full statement checklist. Matrix star is conjugate transpose, multiplication is matrix multiplication, and convexHull ℝ is the usual real convex hull in the complex plane. Allowing an empty index type is harmless: the determinant and every empty permutation product are 1, giving 1 ∈ {1}. Scratch proofs also verified dimension one, arbitrary diagonal summands, and a non-diagonal 2×2 example with determinant 9i/25 in conv{0,i}. Tests in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, reindex.lean, and dimension_two.lean compiled successfully without using the conjecture theorem. The cited source records no resolution conflicting with the open tag. The original de Oliveira publisher link returned HTTP 403, but the cited Wikipedia statement is explicit enough to settle faithfulness. The reviewed file was not modified.
